An HTTP response discloses data the caller is not entitled to receive: The response includes `databaseUrlPrefix` built from `DATABASE_URL.split("@")[0]`, which for a standard connection string exposes the credential portion before the host, while the masking does not remove that credential disclosure.

Loader replaces the accessible-matters filter matterId:{in:matterIds} with attacker-controlled ?matter=, so a client/attorney/paralegal can list deadlines (titles, due dates, assignees) of matters outside their authorized scope.

An AES-CBC decryption failure (invalid padding) is distinguishable from other failures through an externally observable response (tagged-result), without a prior authentication/integrity check — a CBC padding oracle.
Redirect/navigation to a user-controlled URL with no effective same-origin or exact-allowlist check.

Access is checked on the path document id via canAccessDocument, but the served version is fetched by attacker-controlled ?versionId= with no check that the version's documentId equals the authorized document; a user can download the file content of a version belonging to an unauthorized document/matter.
Attacker-controlled text is compiled as a server-side template.
dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders unescaped, non-literal content directly as HTML without a sanitizer.
A URL-named reference reaches an HTTP client call with no destination allowlist or private-network guard.

Client branch first scopes documents to clientMatterIds but then overwrites where.matterId with attacker-controlled ?matterId=, letting a client enumerate client_shared/public_filing documents belonging to other clients' matters.

Privileged mutation has no durable audit-log record, though this repository's own audit-log convention proves one exists and is reachable.

Loader scopes messages to accessible matters via matterId:{in:matterIds} but then overwrites with attacker-controlled ?matter=, dropping the scope; any authenticated user (incl. clients, who see non-draft, and staff, who see all incl. drafts) can read messages belonging to other users'/matters' private threads.

editDraftMessage/applyDraftMessageEdit looks up and updates a ClientMessage by attacker-supplied messageId with no ownership or matter-access check (only isDraft); any authenticated user, including a client, can overwrite subject/content of another user's private draft.
